## Function Exec Runner

The command interface, its os/exec implementation and the scripted fake.

Behaviour: Declares in runner/runner.go: `type Result struct { Stdout string; Stderr string; Code int }`, `type Runner interface { Run(ctx context.Context, dir string, env []string, name string, args ...string) (Result, error) }`, `type OS struct{}`, `type Call struct { Dir string; Name string; Args []string }` and `type Fake struct { Calls []Call; Script map[string]Result; Errors map[string]string; Default Result }` (plus an unexported mutex). `func Key(name string, args ...string) string` = name and the args joined with single spaces. OS.Run: exec.CommandContext(ctx, name, args...) with Dir = dir, WaitDelay = 500 * time.Millisecond (a killed `sh -c` leaves its child holding the output pipes; without WaitDelay Run waits for that child) and Env = os.Environ() followed by env (nil env adds nothing); stdout and stderr captured whole; a non-zero exit is NOT an error: (Result{out, err, code}, nil); the command cannot start (not found, bad dir) → (Result{Code: -1}, an error beginning "runner: "); ctx done before exit → the process is killed and (Result{Code: -1}, ctx.Err()). Fake.Run appends Call{dir, name, args} and returns: Errors[Key] present → (Result{Code: -1}, errors.New(that text)); Script[Key] present → it; else Default; always nil error otherwise.

Steps:
- produces: Result

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given OS{}.Run(ctx, t.TempDir(), nil, "sh", "-c", "printf hi; printf err >&2; exit 3"); when Run; then Result{Stdout: "hi", Stderr: "err", Code: 3}, error nil
2. given dir := t.TempDir() holding one file f.txt; OS{}.Run(ctx, dir, nil, "sh", "-c", "ls"); when Run; then Stdout "f.txt\n", Code 0
3. given OS{}.Run(ctx, t.TempDir(), []string{"MORPH_X=7"}, "sh", "-c", "echo $MORPH_X$HOME"); when Run; then Stdout = "7" + os.Getenv("HOME") + "\n" (the parent environment is kept, the given entries appended)
4. given OS{}.Run(ctx, t.TempDir(), nil, "/nonexistent/bin/x"); then OS{}.Run(ctx, "/nonexistent/dir", nil, "sh", "-c", "true"); when Run; then each Result.Code -1 and an error beginning "runner: "
5. given ctx with a 200 ms timeout; OS{}.Run(ctx, t.TempDir(), nil, "sh", "-c", "sleep 5"); when Run; then returns within 2 s with Code -1 and errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded)
6. given f := &Fake{Script: map[string]Result{"git rev-parse HEAD": {Stdout: "abc\n"}}, Errors: map[string]string{"git fetch -q origin": "runner: fake offline"}, Default: Result{Stdout: "default\n", Code: 4}}; when f.Run(ctx, "/p", nil, "git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"); f.Run(ctx, "/p", nil, "git", "fetch", "-q", "origin"); f.Run(ctx, "/q", nil, "git", "status"); then {Stdout "abc\n", Code 0}, nil; {Code -1} and error text "runner: fake offline"; {Stdout "default\n", Code 4} (the Default), nil; f.Calls == []Call{{"/p", "git", ["rev-parse", "HEAD"]}, {"/p", "git", ["fetch", "-q", "origin"]}, {"/q", "git", ["status"]}}
7. given Key("git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"); Key("morph"); when Key; then "git rev-parse HEAD"; "morph"

## Component requirements / guardrails

Requirements:
- Claude Behind An Interface: The claude CLI is reached only through claude.Process (stdin lines in, stdout lines out, an exit status); the daemon's tests use claude.Fake fed with lines from tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl, never a real claude.
- Bearer Token On Every Route: Every HTTP route but GET /healthz and the MCP endpoints requires Authorization: Bearer <MORPHD_TOKEN>; /mcp and /mcp/{project} require the same token; /mcp/{project}/session requires that project's current session token. morphd listens on 127.0.0.1 only; TLS and the public name are Caddy's.
- The Session Reports Only Itself: A VPS session can call phase_done, wait_operator and milestone only through its own endpoint /mcp/{project}/session with the token morphd minted for that spawn; the token changes on every spawn, so a past session or another project cannot report.

Guardrails:
- Injected Clock And Ids: No package but cmd/morphd reads the clock or a random source: time comes in as a `now` argument or an injected Now func() time.Time, ids from an injected NewID func() string; time.Now, math/rand and crypto/rand appear only in cmd/morphd. Timers are the daemon's Tick, driven by main's ticker.
- No Network In Tests: Tests never open a listener or dial: HTTP is tested with httptest.NewRecorder and httptest.NewRequest, Telegram and GitHub through an injected Do, the MCP server over in-memory transports; a test writes files only under t.TempDir(); no test runs claude or reaches github.com or api.telegram.org.
- No Shell Outside Runner: os/exec is imported only by package runner (git, morph) and package claude (the claude process); every other package runs commands through runner.Runner and tests script them with runner.Fake.
- Secrets Never Logged: The API token, the session tokens, the GitHub token and the Telegram token never appear in a response body, a log line, a milestone, an error text or the argv of a spawned process; secrets live in files of mode 0600 under the state directory; the git credentials reach git through a credential store file, never through a URL or an argument.

Write the files: `runner/runner.go`.

Go 1.22, the standard library only (go.mod requires nothing; the build runs with GOPROXY=off). gofmt-formatted (gofmt -l prints nothing) and go vet clean. A file's package is its directory's base name; exported names in MixedCaps; a package imports another of the module by the module path of go.mod + "/" + its directory. Tests are `func TestXxx(t *testing.T)` in the package's own `_test.go` files, table tests allowed; compare with `testhelp.Equal(t, what, got, want)` of the module's `internal/testhelp`, never your own helper; no t.Skip, no network, no clock, no goroutine left running.

## Function Parse Event

One output line of the claude stream decoded into the Event the rest of morphd reads.

Behaviour: Declares in stream/parse.go, exactly, one field per line: `type Question struct { Text string `json:"text"`; Header string `json:"header"`; Options []string `json:"options"`; MultiSelect bool `json:"multi_select"`; ToolUseID string `json:"tool_use_id"` }`; `type Result struct { Subtype string `json:"subtype"`; IsError bool `json:"is_error"`; NumTurns int `json:"num_turns"`; TotalCostUSD float64 `json:"total_cost_usd"`; TerminalReason string `json:"terminal_reason"`; DurationMS int64 `json:"duration_ms"`; Errors []string `json:"errors"` }`; `type Window struct { Utilization float64 `json:"utilization"`; ResetsAt int64 `json:"resets_at"` }`; `type Limits struct { FiveHour Window `json:"five_hour"`; SevenDay Window `json:"seven_day"` }`; `type Event struct { Type string `json:"type"`; Subtype string `json:"subtype"`; SessionID string `json:"session_id"`; RequestID string `json:"request_id"`; Tool string `json:"tool"`; Text string `json:"text"`; Question *Question `json:"question,omitempty"`; Result *Result `json:"result,omitempty"`; Limits *Limits `json:"limits,omitempty"`; Input json.RawMessage `json:"input,omitempty"`; Raw json.RawMessage `json:"-"` }` and `func Parse(line []byte) (Event, error)`. Parse trims white space; an empty line → error "stream: empty line"; invalid JSON → an error whose text begins "stream: bad json"; valid JSON that is not an object → "stream: not an object"; an object without a string "type" → "stream: no type". Otherwise Raw = the trimmed line, Type = "type", SessionID = the top-level "session_id" when present, and by Type: "system" → Subtype = "subtype"; "assistant" → Text = the "text" of every content part of message.content with part type "text", joined with "\n" (thinking and tool_use parts contribute nothing); "result" → Subtype = "subtype", Text = the "result" string when present, Result filled from subtype, is_error, num_turns, total_cost_usd, terminal_reason, duration_ms and errors (absent errors → nil); "rate_limit_event" → Limits from rate_limit_info.unifiedWindows.five_hour / seven_day (utilization, resetsAt), a missing window leaves its Window zero; "control_request" → RequestID = "request_id", Subtype = request.subtype, and when the subtype is "can_use_tool": Tool = request.tool_name, Input = the raw bytes of request.input, and when Tool is "AskUserQuestion" and input.questions has at least one element: Question from the first element (question, header, the label of every option, multiSelect) with ToolUseID = request.tool_use_id; "control_response" → RequestID = response.request_id, Subtype = response.subtype. Any other Type passes through with only Type, SessionID and Raw set. Unknown keys are ignored everywhere.

Steps:
- produces: Event

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given the msg bytes of line 4 of tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl (dir out, a system init); then line 16 (a control_response to int-1); when Parse; then Event{Type: "system", Subtype: "init", SessionID: "967e8f4d-a2eb-4aa6-968b-b9054a1c3d7e"}, Question, Result, Limits nil, Text "", error nil; then Event{Type: "control_response", Subtype: "success", RequestID: "int-1"} with SessionID "" (ref: tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl)
2. given line 5 (assistant text PONG); line 12 (assistant with one thinking part); line 13 (assistant with one tool_use part); when Parse; then Text "PONG", Type "assistant", SessionID "967e8f4d-a2eb-4aa6-968b-b9054a1c3d7e"; then Text ""; then Text "" — only text parts count; all three error nil (ref: tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl)
3. given line 6 (rate_limit_event); when Parse; then Type "rate_limit_event", Limits &Limits{FiveHour: Window{Utilization: 0.22, ResetsAt: 1791469200}, SevenDay: Window{Utilization: 0.6, ResetsAt: 1791853200}}, Result nil (ref: tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl)
4. given line 7 (the result of the PONG turn); when Parse; then Type "result", Subtype "success", Text "PONG", Result &Result{Subtype: "success", IsError: false, NumTurns: 1, TotalCostUSD: 0.0021784900000000004, TerminalReason: "completed", DurationMS: 958, Errors: nil}, Limits nil (ref: tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl)
5. given line 19 (the result after the interrupt); when Parse; then Result &Result{Subtype: "error_during_execution", IsError: true, NumTurns: 3, TotalCostUSD: 0.0028906000000000005, TerminalReason: "aborted_streaming", DurationMS: 3032, Errors: []string{"[ede_diagnostic] result_type=user last_content_type=n/a stop_reason=tool_use"}}, Text "" (ref: tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl)
6. given line 27 (control_request can_use_tool for AskUserQuestion); when Parse; then Type "control_request", Subtype "can_use_tool", RequestID "9f4ffa22-2676-4391-bfd9-bd7d16c3866c", Tool "AskUserQuestion", Question &Question{Text: "Which option do you want: A or B?", Header: "A or B", Options: []string{"Option A", "Option B"}, MultiSelect: false, ToolUseID: "toolu_01FUdZWoHspVQKBCdwkjgj1R"}, and Input decodes (json.Unmarshal into map[string]any) to the same value as the line's request.input (ref: tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl)
7. given the literal line {"type":"control_request","request_id":"r-7","request":{"subtype":"can_use_tool","tool_name":"Bash","input":{"command":"ls"},"tool_use_id":"toolu_x"}}; when Parse; then RequestID "r-7", Tool "Bash", Question nil, Input exactly the bytes {"command":"ls"}, SessionID ""
8. given in turn the lines "" , " \n", "[1,2]", "{\"a\":1}", "{\"type\":\"result\"" (cut), "{\"type\":7}"; when Parse; then errors with texts "stream: empty line", "stream: empty line", "stream: not an object", "stream: no type", one beginning "stream: bad json", "stream: no type"; every Event zero

Data Event: One parsed output line of claude.
Schema:
type Event struct { Type, Subtype, SessionID, RequestID, Tool, Text string; Question *Question; Result *Result; Limits *Limits; Input json.RawMessage; Raw json.RawMessage }

## Function Phase Queue

Load a plan with defaults, walk it phase by phase, stop and continue by the plan's marks.

Behaviour: Declares in queue/queue.go, exactly: `type Caps struct { ClaudeUSD float64 `json:"claude_usd"`; Hours float64 `json:"hours"`; ExecutorUSD float64 `json:"executor_usd"` }`; `type Phase struct { ID string `json:"id"`; StopAfter string `json:"stop_after"`; Caps Caps `json:"caps"` }`; `type Plan struct { Approved string `json:"approved"`; Phases []Phase `json:"phases"` }`; `type Outcome struct { Next string `json:"next"`; Stop string `json:"stop"` }`; `type Queue struct { Approved string `json:"approved"`; Phases []Phase `json:"phases"`; Index int `json:"index"`; State string `json:"state"`; Reason string `json:"reason"` }`; `func Load(p Plan, defaults Caps) (Queue, error)`, `func (q *Queue) Current() (Phase, bool)`, `func (q *Queue) Start() (Phase, error)`, `func (q *Queue) Done(phase, next string) (Outcome, error)`, `func (q *Queue) Stop(reason string)`, `func (q *Queue) Continue() (Phase, error)`. State is one of "empty", "queued", "running", "stopped", "done"; a zero Queue has State "" and Current false. Load: Approved trimmed must be non-empty → "queue: approved hash required"; no phases → "queue: no phases"; each ID trimmed non-empty → "queue: phase <i>: empty id" (i from 0); repeated → "queue: duplicate phase \"<id>\""; StopAfter "" becomes "none", else must be "none", "smoke" or "operator" → "queue: phase \"<id>\": stop_after \"<v>\""; each zero Caps field is filled from defaults. The result has State "queued", Index 0. Current: the phase at Index when State is "queued", "running" or "stopped" and Index < len(Phases). Start: "queued" → State "running", returns Current; else error "queue: cannot start in state \"<s>\"". Done: State must be "running" and phase == Current().ID else error "queue: phase_done for \"<phase>\" but running \"<id>\"" (an empty running id when none); next must equal the ID of the phase after Index, or "" when there is none, else "queue: next \"<next>\", plan says \"<id>\"" (plan says "" when none); then Index++ and: no phase left → State "done", Outcome{Stop: "end"}; the finished phase's StopAfter "none" → State "queued", Outcome{Next: that id}; "smoke" or "operator" → State "stopped", Reason = StopAfter, Outcome{Next: that id, Stop: StopAfter}. Stop: State "running" or "queued" → "stopped" with Reason (Index unchanged); otherwise nothing. Continue: "stopped" → State "queued", Reason "", returns Current (error "queue: nothing to continue (state \"<s>\")" when Current is false or the state differs).

Steps:
- produces: Plan

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given the Plan decoded from tests/fixtures/plan/queue-3.json (3 phases: P17 none, P18 smoke with caps {claude_usd 12}, P19 none); defaults Caps{30, 3, 5}; when Load; then error nil; State "queued", Index 0, Approved "7b31dfe"; Phases[0] {ID "P17", StopAfter "none", Caps {30, 3, 5}}; Phases[1] {ID "P18", StopAfter "smoke", Caps {12, 3, 5}}; Phases[2].StopAfter "none"; Current() = P17, true (ref: tests/fixtures/plan/queue-3.json)
2. given Plan{Approved: " "}; Plan{Approved: "h", Phases: nil}; Plan{Approved: "h", Phases: [{ID " "}]}; Plan{Approved: "h", Phases: [{ID "P1"}, {ID "P1"}]}; Plan{Approved: "h", Phases: [{ID "P1", StopAfter: "pause"}]}; when Load; then errors "queue: approved hash required"; "queue: no phases"; "queue: phase 0: empty id"; "queue: duplicate phase \"P1\""; "queue: phase \"P1\": stop_after \"pause\""
3. given the queue of example 1; when Start(); Start() again; Done("P17", "P18"); then P17, nil; error "queue: cannot start in state \"running\""; Outcome{Next: "P18"}, nil, State "queued", Index 1, Current() P18 (ref: tests/fixtures/plan/queue-3.json)
4. given the queue after example 3 (queued at P18); Start(); when Done("P17", "P19"); Done("P18", "P17"); Done("P18", "P19"); then error "queue: phase_done for \"P17\" but running \"P18\""; error "queue: next \"P17\", plan says \"P19\""; Outcome{Next: "P19", Stop: "smoke"}, State "stopped", Reason "smoke", Index 2 (ref: tests/fixtures/plan/queue-3.json)
5. given the stopped queue after example 4; when Done("P19", ""); Continue(); Start(); Done("P19", ""); then error "queue: phase_done for \"P19\" but running \"\""; P19, nil with State "queued" and Reason ""; P19, nil; Outcome{Stop: "end"}, State "done", Index 3, Current() false (ref: tests/fixtures/plan/queue-3.json)
6. given a running queue at P17; Stop("not pushed"); when Stop, then Continue(), then Done("P17", "P18") without Start; then State "stopped", Reason "not pushed", Index 0; Continue → P17 and State "queued"; Done → error "queue: phase_done for \"P17\" but running \"\""
7. given a done queue; a zero Queue{}; when Continue(); Stop("x"); Current(); then error "queue: nothing to continue (state \"done\")"; the done queue unchanged; the zero queue: Current false, Continue error "queue: nothing to continue (state \"\")"
8. given Plan{Approved: "abc", Phases: [{ID "P1", StopAfter: "operator", Caps: {Hours: 1}}]}, defaults {20, 2, 4}; when Load; Start; Done("P1", ""); then Caps {20, 1, 4}; Outcome{Stop: "end"} (no next phase wins over stop_after), State "done"

Data Plan: What plan_load carries.
Schema:
type Plan struct { Approved string `json:"approved"`; Phases []Phase `json:"phases"` }

## Function Encode Lines

The input lines morphd writes to claude, each one JSON object ending with a newline.

Behaviour: Declares in stream/encode.go: `func Initialize(requestID string) []byte`, `func Interrupt(requestID string) []byte`, `func User(text string) []byte`, `func Allow(requestID string, input json.RawMessage) ([]byte, error)` and `func Answer(requestID string, input json.RawMessage, question, label string) ([]byte, error)`. Every line is the json.Marshal of a struct whose fields are declared in the order written below (encoding/json's HTML escaping stays on, so < > & become \u003c \u003e \u0026) followed by exactly one "\n". Initialize: {"type":"control_request","request_id":<id>,"request":{"subtype":"initialize"}}. Interrupt: the same with subtype "interrupt". User: {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":<text>},"parent_tool_use_id":null}. Allow: {"type":"control_response","response":{"subtype":"success","request_id":<id>,"response":{"behavior":"allow","updatedInput":<input>}}} where input is embedded as json.RawMessage (so it is compacted); an input that is not valid JSON → (nil, an error whose text begins "stream: bad input"). Answer: input must decode (json.Unmarshal) into map[string]any, else (nil, "stream: input is not an object"); the map gets the key "answers" = map[string]string{question: label} (replacing any existing "answers") and is embedded as updatedInput by json.Marshal (so object keys come out sorted at every level, as encoding/json writes maps); the rest as Allow.

Steps:
- produces: json line

Examples (the tests must prove each one):
1. given requestID "init-1"; then "init-2"; when Initialize; then exactly {"type":"control_request","request_id":"init-1","request":{"subtype":"initialize"}} + "\n"; then the same with "init-2"
2. given requestID "int-1"; then "int-9"; when Interrupt; then exactly {"type":"control_request","request_id":"int-1","request":{"subtype":"interrupt"}} + "\n"; then with "int-9"
3. given text "Reply with exactly one word: PONG"; when User; then exactly {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"Reply with exactly one word: PONG"},"parent_tool_use_id":null} + "\n", which decodes equal (map[string]any) to the msg of line 3 of tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl (ref: tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl)
4. given text "a <b> & \"c\"\nd" (a Go string with a real newline); when User; then exactly {"type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":"a \u003cb\u003e \u0026 \"c\"\nd"},"parent_tool_use_id":null} + "\n" (the <, >, & and \n are six-character and two-character escapes in the bytes; in a Go test the want is a raw string literal, since an interpreted Go string would turn the six-character escapes back into < > &)
5. given requestID "r-7", input {"command": "ls"} (with the space); when Allow; then exactly {"type":"control_response","response":{"subtype":"success","request_id":"r-7","response":{"behavior":"allow","updatedInput":{"command":"ls"}}}} + "\n", error nil
6. given requestID "r-1", input {"questions":[{"question":"Q?","options":[{"label":"Yes"},{"label":"No"}]}]}, question "Q?", label "Yes"; when Answer; then exactly {"type":"control_response","response":{"subtype":"success","request_id":"r-1","response":{"behavior":"allow","updatedInput":{"answers":{"Q?":"Yes"},"questions":[{"options":[{"label":"Yes"},{"label":"No"}],"question":"Q?"}]}}}} + "\n", error nil
7. given requestID "9f4ffa22-2676-4391-bfd9-bd7d16c3866c", input = request.input of line 27 of tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl, question "Which option do you want: A or B?", label "Option B"; when Answer; then error nil; the line decodes (map[string]any) equal to the msg of line 28 (the probe's own answer, dir in) (ref: tests/fixtures/stream/probe.jsonl)
8. given Answer with input [1]; Allow with input {"a": (cut); when called; then (nil, error "stream: input is not an object"); (nil, an error beginning "stream: bad input")

- Bearer Token On Every Route: Every HTTP route but GET /healthz and the MCP endpoints requires Authorization: Bearer <MORPHD_TOKEN>; /mcp and /mcp/{project} require the same token; /mcp/{project}/session requires that project's current session token. morphd listens on 127.0.0.1 only; TLS and the public name are Caddy's.
- The Session Reports Only Itself: A VPS session can call phase_done, wait_operator and milestone only through its own endpoint /mcp/{project}/session with the token morphd minted for that spawn; the token changes on every spawn, so a past session or another project cannot report.

Guardrails:
- Injected Clock And Ids: No package but cmd/morphd reads the clock or a random source: time comes in as a `now` argument or an injected Now func() time.Time, ids from an injected NewID func() string; time.Now, math/rand and crypto/rand appear only in cmd/morphd. Timers are the daemon's Tick, driven by main's ticker.
- No Network In Tests: Tests never open a listener or dial: HTTP is tested with httptest.NewRecorder and httptest.NewRequest, Telegram and GitHub through an injected Do, the MCP server over in-memory transports; a test writes files only under t.TempDir(); no test runs claude or reaches github.com or api.telegram.org.
- No Shell Outside Runner: os/exec is imported only by package runner (git, morph) and package claude (the claude process); every other package runs commands through runner.Runner and tests script them with runner.Fake.
- Secrets Never Logged: The API token, the session tokens, the GitHub token and the Telegram token never appear in a response body, a log line, a milestone, an error text or the argv of a spawned process; secrets live in files of mode 0600 under the state directory; the git credentials reach git through a credential store file, never through a URL or an argument.
